source_name: Gránit Bank careers
why_relevant: Fast-growing digital-first HU bank; headcount adds in digital product/engineering are a leading indicator of its expansion and acquisitions integration.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary careers / internships
why_relevant: Large foreign-owned HU bank; its own site carries internship and role information, while the bulk of ads route to the group Workday/board postings - useful for cross-checking group vs local hiring.

source_name: Wise (wise.jobs) Budapest office board
why_relevant: Wise's Budapest hub is one of the largest foreign payments employers in HU; its tagged Budapest feed shows engineering/ops/risk build-out and stable per-job IDs make diffing easy.

source_name: Indeed Hungary (hu.indeed.com) employer-scoped queries
why_relevant: Broad aggregator that surfaces ads from banks and their staffing agencies that never appear on the bank's own site; result counts per employer give a cheap volume proxy.

source_name: Jooble Hungary (hu.jooble.org) keyword feeds
why_relevant: Meta-aggregator that indexes smaller HU boards and agency sites; useful as a discovery net for boards not yet in the inventory, and for AML/payments keyword volume in Budapest.

source_name: Greenhouse job boards (job-boards.greenhouse.io / boards.eu.greenhouse.io) filtered to Budapest
why_relevant: Foreign fintechs and payment vendors with Budapest hubs commonly publish on Greenhouse; boards expose a predictable JSON endpoint per company token, making structured, ToS-friendly collection possible.

source_name: Lever job boards (jobs.lever.co / jobs.eu.lever.co) with Budapest postings
why_relevant: Second common ATS among payment/crypto-payment firms; same token-per-company structure allows a uniform Budapest filter across many employers.

source_name: SmartRecruiters public job search filtered to Hungary
why_relevant: Cross-tenant search over all SmartRecruiters customers, so a single query surfaces HU postings from employers whose ATS tenant is otherwise unknown - a discovery channel as well as a feed.

source_name: LinkedIn Jobs Hungary company pages (hu.linkedin.com/jobs/<company>-jobs)
why_relevant: Often the only place foreign fintechs post HU roles, and it ties vacancies to named hiring managers - the bridge between vacancy data and leadership-move tracking. Heavily gated, so treat as observational.

source_name: Simplejob.com company pages (HU aggregator, e.g. OTP Bank)
why_relevant: Small HU aggregator organised by company (ceg = company) with nationwide branch-level roles - good for branch-network expansion/contraction signals that head-office ATS pages under-represent.

source_name: BankWeb.hu banki állás directory
why_relevant: Sector-specific HU directory linking bank career pages in one place - a cheap way to complete the inventory of smaller banks, savings co-ops and financial enterprises whose careers pages are otherwise hard to find.

source_name: Hays Hungary — Salary Guide (Hays Bérfelmérés / Fizetési útmutató)
why_relevant: Annual Hungarian salary guide built on a Hays Hungary survey (2026 edition cited as 4,200+ employer/employee respondents, 600+ positions, 14 industries) with a dedicated finance/banking sector chapter. Gives salary bands, wage-increase expectations and scarcity commentary that quantify banking and payments hiring demand in HU. Also flags the 2026 mandatory pay-transparency shift, which will reshape how banks publish salary ranges in job ads.

source_name: Hays Hungary Salary Guide 2026 — full PDF (Pénzcentrum CDN mirror)
why_relevant: An apparently ungated PDF copy of the full 2026 Hays Hungary salary guide hosted by a Hungarian business news site — the fastest route to the actual numeric salary tables (including finance/banking roles) without passing Hays' lead-capture gate.

source_name: Randstad Hungary — Bérpiaci iránytű (salary-market compass) and Bérfelmérés
why_relevant: Randstad HU's paid/commissioned salary-benchmark products plus the free positioning material around them. Reveals which functions Randstad considers scarce and how it segments the Hungarian white-collar market; the company also runs 100+ consultants covering junior-to-top-management placements, giving a live view of demand.

source_name: Randstad Hungary — Workforce Insights / Toborzás content hub
why_relevant: Randstad's Hungarian editorial hub on recruitment trends — the channel where its Employer Brand Research and hiring-trend commentary land in Hungarian. Useful for narrative signals about which sectors (incl. finance/SSC/banking back office) are staffing up or freezing.

source_name: ManpowerGroup Hungary — Munkaerőpiaci Előrejelzés (Employment Outlook Survey, MEOS)
why_relevant: Quarterly net-employment-outlook survey with an explicit 'pénzügy és biztosítás' (finance & insurance) sector cut for Hungary — one of very few recurring, sector-broken-out, quantified hiring-intent series for HU banking/insurance. Search results show finance/insurance NEO readings such as +27% and +19% in recent quarters.

source_name: Trenkwalder Magyarország — Hírek / Bérbarométer press-release series
why_relevant: Trenkwalder publishes a recurring quarterly wage barometer built on its own payroll/staffing base (~7,000 employees), heavily picked up by Hungarian business media. Its core is blue-collar hourly wages, so it is a weak direct signal for banking, but it is the benchmark labour-cost baseline against which banking/BPO salary claims are read, and it occasionally covers white-collar and Budapest-region tightness.

source_name: Amrop Hungary (Amrop Kohlmann & Young) — firm site and consultant profiles
why_relevant: One of the longest-established retained executive search firms in Hungary (since 1992) with Financial Services as a declared practice; managing partners Richard Kohlmann and Katalin Indra Hollai both list Financial Services coverage. Consultant pages, insight posts and LinkedIn activity indirectly reveal which Hungarian banks/insurers are running board- and C-level mandates.

source_name: Stanton Chase Budapest — executive search, finance practice
why_relevant: Global retained search firm with a Budapest office explicitly claiming strength in finance; publishes market commentary and leadership-appointment notes that indirectly disclose Hungarian financial-institution senior hiring.

source_name: HumanField Vezető- és Specialistakiválasztó Kft.
why_relevant: Hungarian-owned executive/specialist search firm repeatedly ranked at or near the top of the BBJ headhunter toplist, with a declared financial-sector practice (search results show it recruiting insurance regional-director roles). Its live vacancy list is a direct, named-role window on Hungarian financial-services senior demand — employers stay anonymous but the role, region and package do not.

source_name: Beck & Partners (bap.hu) — Executive Search Hungary
source_subtype: executive search firm site / job board
why_relevant: Established Hungarian headhunting/online-recruitment firm; its executive-search pages and job board carry Hungarian-language senior mandates, useful for tracking C-level and head-of-function demand at Hungarian financial institutions.

source_name: HR Portál — fejvadászat / executive search tag and annual headhunter toplist
source_subtype: trade media tag feed / ranking coverage
why_relevant: The main Hungarian HR trade outlet. Its 'fejvadász' tag and its recurring 'legnagyobb vezetőkiválasztó cégek' articles reproduce the BBJ executive-search revenue ranking — the single best pointer for enumerating the actor set (ISG International Executive Consulting, Amrop Kohlmann & Young, PSP Siklóssy & Partner, Kienbaum Executive Consultants, HILL International, HumanField) and for tracking which firms are gaining share, a proxy for where senior hiring money flows.

source_name: Budapest Business Journal — Book of Lists (executive search / recruitment rankings)
why_relevant: The primary underlying dataset behind every Hungarian headhunter ranking: BBJ compiles revenue-based toplists of executive search and recruitment firms annually. Buying the Book of Lists gives a complete, ordered actor map for this cell rather than the partial top-10 reproduced in free media.

source_name: Michael Page / PageGroup — Banking & Financial Services Salary Guide (regional, HU served from Vienna)
why_relevant: PageGroup publishes a dedicated Banking & Financial Services salary guide plus an annual global Salary Guide. Hungary has no Michael Page office — CEE incl. HU is covered from Vienna — so this is a regional-context source rather than an HU-native one, but it is useful for cross-border pay comparison and for spotting where HU banking talent is being pulled toward Austria/DACH.

source_name: Enloyd — Salary Guide 2026 (Hungary)
why_relevant: A CEE recruitment consultancy publishing a Hungary-focused 2026 salary guide covering salary trends plus the economic/technology developments shaping the HU labour market. A second, independent salary-band series to triangulate against Hays for finance/SSC/banking roles.

source_name: Grafton Recruitment Hungary — Salary & Market Guide
why_relevant: Grafton (Gi Group Holding) is a major HU white-collar/SSC recruiter and historically published a Salary & Market Guide covering business-services and finance roles; it also co-authored a business-services-sector salary guide with Hays and Trenkwalder. Budapest's banking back-office and SSC hiring is a core Grafton segment, so its guide is directly on-topic for payments/finance operations roles.

source_name: ISG International Executive Consulting Kft. (Hungary)
why_relevant: Named by the BBJ/HR Portál ranking as one of the largest executive search firms operating in Hungary. Its Hungarian mandate listings and press activity indirectly indicate senior financial-services vacancies. URL form inferred from the ranking coverage — needs manual confirmation of the exact HU domain.

source_name: Horton International Hungary — executive search Budapest
why_relevant: Global search network with a Hungary practice; another node for detecting senior financial-services mandates and appointment announcements in Budapest.
